source_name: CeJN Crna Gora - official Facebook page
why_relevant: Operational announcement channel for the portal: outages, migrations, new modules, deadline changes and training. Cheap early-warning signal that a collector's assumptions about CeJN structure are about to break.

source_name: Čistoća d.o.o. Podgorica (waste utility)
why_relevant: Podgorica waste-collection utility and a buyer in the municipal SOE layer. No independent website surfaced in this pass; its public communication runs largely through Facebook, and it is represented on the Chamber of Commerce utility association board. Track mainly via CeJN and the chamber association rather than a self-published tender page.

source_name: Komunalne usluge d.o.o. Podgorica (municipal utility services)
why_relevant: City-owned utility (public lighting, traffic signalling and related communal services) founded by the Podgorica city assembly. Represents the municipal-SOE buyer layer that procures locally and publishes on its own site. Lower payments intensity than EPCG/Pošta, but part of the complete buyer map for the cell.

source_name: Montenegro-focused commercial tender aggregators (montenegrotenders.com, tendersontime, globaltenders, tendersinfo)
why_relevant: English-language commercial mirrors of Montenegrin tender flow. Low intrinsic credibility and heavy paywalling, but useful for English keyword discovery, for spotting notices whose Montenegrin wording our glossary misses, and as an availability cross-check when CeJN is unreachable.

source_name: MontenegroTenders.com
why_relevant: English-language Montenegro-only commercial tender database claiming daily harvesting from official procurement portals, government sites, ministries, local authorities, private authorities and newspapers. Value is the newspaper/private-authority layer and English normalisation for non-local analysts; quality claims are unverified and typical of the Indian-operated tender-aggregator family.

source_name: Advokatska kancelarija Duraković (Bar, ME) - local law firm with procurement practice
why_relevant: Example of the domestic law-firm layer that publishes practitioner commentary in Montenegrin on procurement procedures and remedies. Domestic-firm commentary is the sr-language counterpart to international guides and often flags bylaw-level problems earlier.

source_name: Antena M (antenam.net) — independent Podgorica radio and news portal
why_relevant: Independent Podgorica-based broadcaster confirmed to exist and operate antenam.net. Known for combative political and accountability coverage, so a plausible carrier of procurement-affair reporting, but no procurement article surfaced in this run — carried as a low-confidence monitoring candidate.

source_name: ASK on X/Twitter (@ASK_CrnaGora)
why_relevant: Low-latency announcement channel for ASK findings and report publication, useful as a trigger for pulling the underlying PDF rather than polling the site.

source_name: dddInvoices - Electronic Fiscalization and E-Invoicing in Montenegro
why_relevant: Second independent commercial tracker covering both Montenegrin electronic fiscalisation (already live) and the pending e-invoicing mandate; useful to triangulate dates and to understand how fiscalisation infrastructure interacts with any B2G e-invoicing obligation.

source_name: dgMarket — aggregated donor tender notices
why_relevant: Cross-donor aggregator carrying World Bank, EU, UN and national donor notices in one place. Useful as a recall safety net and for retrospective searching when a donor portal has poor archives; not authoritative and partly paywalled, so treat as secondary.

source_name: erstegroupprocurement.com (EGP vanity domain, 301 to erstegroup.com)
why_relevant: Canonical vanity domain cited in third-party profiles as the EGP website. Observed to 301-redirect to the erstegroup.com procurement page, so it is a stable alias worth pinning in a monitor list; if EGP ever stands up a standalone supplier portal it will most likely reappear here.

source_name: GlobalTenders — Montenegro tenders
why_relevant: Aggregator that states it ingests Montenegrin authority websites, newspapers, journals and magazines and applies AI/ML normalisation and de-duplication. The stated newspaper/journal ingestion is the differentiator worth testing, since low-value or legacy notices still appear in print in ME.

source_name: Lovćen banka AD Podgorica – corporate website
why_relevant: Domestic bank named in the cell scope; same rationale as other independents — direct sourcing of core banking/cards/ATM. Not confirmed in this run.

source_name: Opentender.eu (DIGIWHIST / Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: EU-funded transparency scraper covering ~33-35 jurisdictions (TED + national portals) with red-flag indicators and downloadable datasets. Montenegro does NOT appear in its stated coverage (Serbia and North Macedonia do), so its main value here is (a) a regional benchmark for RS/MK against which ME can be compared, and (b) reusable open-source scraping/analytics code on GitHub.

source_name: Pazar3.me – classifieds, IT jobs section
why_relevant: High-volume Montenegrin classifieds site carrying IT vacancies (programmers, project managers, DBAs) including from banks and their integrators; complements the formal job boards and catches smaller vendors that do not post elsewhere.

source_name: Porto Montenegro events calendar (INFINTECH host venue)
why_relevant: Venue-side listing confirms event dates and sometimes lists partner organisations before the event's own site updates — a secondary confirmation channel for the conference-signal stream.

source_name: tenderi.hr — Crna Gora section (Croatian sister platform)
why_relevant: Croatian-market bid-alert product with a Montenegro cross-border module; likely the same backend as javne-nabavke.com. Useful mainly as a duplicate-coverage check and for its FAQ, which documents source lists and update cadence (a rare disclosure of aggregator methodology).

source_name: TendersGo — Montenegro tracking pages
why_relevant: Smaller SEO-driven aggregator publishing Montenegro sector-tracking posts. Low standalone value, but its public posts occasionally name specific contracting authorities and sectors, which is useful for actor-map snowballing without a subscription.

source_name: TendersInfo — Montenegro & Balkan region tenders
why_relevant: Long-running global tender database with Montenegro and Balkan-region country cuts and customised e-mail alerts; claims both government and private tenders. Relevant chiefly as a third redundancy layer and for its historical archive, which often outlives deleted national notices.

source_name: Western Union Montenegro — agent network page
why_relevant: Reveals the remittance distribution partnership map in Montenegro. Search results named the agent set as Pošta Crne Gore plus banks (Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Komercijalna, Lovćen, Podgorička, Prva, UCB, Ziraat), mobile operator MTEL and bus stations, with the WU principal role held since 2015 by payment institution Montenegro Transfers doo. Agent-network changes are partner-selection events for this cell.
